name: Ukrainian alert API ecosystem: alerts.in.ua API (+ official Python client alerts-ua/alerts-in-ua-py) and UkraineAlarm API (api.ukrainealarm.com) with PaulAnnekov/uasiren (siren.pp.ua public wrapper) and PaulAnnekov/ukrainealarm

popularity: alerts-in-ua-py 29 stars / 3 forks; PaulAnnekov/ukrainealarm 36 stars; uasiren 27 stars / 2 forks; FOUREX/alerts_in_ua.py (unofficial) 11 stars; Fyennyi/alerts-in-ua-php 6 stars; UkraineAlarm official generated clients 2-3 stars (all as of 2026-10-17).
peer_review_status: Not peer-reviewed. Operational public-alert APIs and volunteer/official client libraries; accuracy self-reported; alerts.in.ua disclaims liability and warns updates may be delayed and must not be used for critical infrastructure.
target_type: Not applicable (data APIs). They expose alert intervals (history) and current state (active/IoT), from which our ONSET target is built; IoT status strings are pure STATE snapshots and cannot give onsets unless polled continuously.
target_definition: Not applicable. Record unit (alerts.in.ua): one alert for one location with id, started_at, finished_at (null if open), updated_at, alert_type, alert_level (red/yellow), location_type, location_uid, location_oblast. UkraineAlarm: per region activeAlerts[] with type (AIR, ARTILLERY, URBAN_FIGHTS, ...) and activeAlertLevels[] (alertLevel Red/Yellow, createdAt).
spatial_unit: alerts.in.ua: oblast, raion, hromada, city (history dump 2026-10-12: raion 14,366, hromada 1,080, city 1,072, oblast 221 rows); queried per oblast UID. UkraineAlarm/siren.pp.ua: State / District / Community regionType with regionId.
at_risk_masking: Not applicable (APIs). For users: the history endpoint returns open alerts too (41 open in our dump, incl. Luhansk since 2022-04-04 and Crimea since 2022-12-10, and multi-year Vovchanska/Lypetska hromada alerts), so at-risk masks must apply the D-020 causal 24h cap rather than 'finished_at is null'.
data_sources: alerts.in.ua history: /v1/regions/{uid}/alerts/month_ago.json (only documented period; the Python client default 'week_ago' is NOT in the docs [uncertain whether still served]). Our dump 2026-10-12T16:45Z: 26 oblast UIDs returned 200 (UIDs 6 and 7 returned 404), 16,739 records, 0 duplicate ids, closed alerts finished from 2026-09-12 16:52 UTC (exactly 30 days before fetch) and started from 2026-09-11 05:50 UTC. Live: /v1/alerts/active.json (with threats[]), /v1|v2/iot/active_air_raid_alerts*.json. UkraineAlarm: /api/v3/alerts, /api/v3/alerts/{regionId}, /api/v3/alerts/status (lastActionIndex), /api/v3/regions, /api/v3/alerts/regionHistory?regionId= (last 25 alerts of a region only). siren.pp.ua mirrors /alerts, /alerts/{id}, /alerts/status, /regions without a key.
data_source_variant: Three distinct channels, never to be mixed with each other or with Vadimkin official_data (Telegram air_alert_ua parse): (1) alerts.in.ua (own aggregation; has alert_level, threats, location_title_en, updated_at); (2) UkraineAlarm API (feeds the official 'Povitriana Tryvoha' app; key on request; Red/Yellow activeAlertLevels since the Sep-2026 reform); (3) siren.pp.ua = keyless public proxy of (2), 50 req/min per IP. All are union-of-levels-capable (oblast/raion/hromada rows) but only alerts.in.ua offers a 30-day bulk history; UkraineAlarm history is capped at 25 alerts per region.
preprocessing: Needed on the user side (verified on our 2026-10-12 dump): (a) filter alert_type == 'air_raid' (288 artillery_shelling + 1 urban_fights rows present); (b) map rows to oblast by the REQUESTED oblast UID or the location_oblast name, NOT location_oblast_uid: in our dump location_oblast_uid equals the row's own location_uid for every raion/hromada/city row (16,518 rows), i.e. the field is not the oblast UID; (c) dedupe by id keeping latest updated_at across dumps (D-027); (d) keep open alerts and apply the D-020 24h causal cap; (e) drop Luhansk (16), Crimea (29), Sevastopol (30); (f) treat the window start as left-censored: the month_ago window appears to filter by finished_at >= fetch-30d [uncertain], so onsets in the first ~1-2 days of the window are incomplete (only long alerts that ended later survive); (g) timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds ('...000Z'); the Python client converts them to Europe/Kyiv-aware datetimes, so convert back to UTC before grid work.
known_label_artefacts: (1) Left-censoring at the 30-day history edge: alerts that started before the window but finished inside it appear (our min started_at 2026-09-11 05:50 vs min finished_at 2026-09-12 16:52), while short alerts from that period are absent; any onset rate from the first day of a dump is biased low. Handling: start the scored window after the earliest finished_at (our project uses 2026-09-13). (2) Open/standing alerts in history (Luhansk 2022-04-04, Crimea 2022-12-10, Vovchanska hromada artillery/urban fights since 2024-05-20, Lypetska hromada air_raid since 2026-03-10): handle with D-020 cap and unit exclusions. (3) Misleading location_oblast_uid (equals location_uid for sub-oblast rows). (4) Mixed alert types (artillery_shelling, urban_fights) in the same endpoint. (5) threats[] only in live active.json and only while a threat is open; history has alert_level but no threats (documented in client README), so threat-type labels cannot be reconstructed historically without continuous polling. (6) Alert-level independence: a yellow alert can carry a red threat; red-only targets based on alert_level will miss red threats inside yellow alerts [uncertain how often]. (7) Latency: UkraineAlarm/siren.pp.ua showed 5-10 min delays in appearance and clearing around 2026-09-14/15 (uasiren #13, ukrainealarm #11) due to a provider rate limit, later lifted; short alerts were lost in HA. Timestamps in payloads stayed correct, so history is fine but live polling-based onset capture can miss short alerts. (8) alerts.in.ua disclaimer: updates may be delayed. (9) No history for 2026-09-07..12 anywhere in this ecosystem as used by us (alerts.in.ua 30-day window had passed; UkraineAlarm keeps only 25 alerts/region).
features: Not applicable. Fields usable for features: alert_level (red/yellow), alert_type, location_type, started_at, finished_at, updated_at (alerts.in.ua); live-only threats[] with threat_type in {drones, ballistic_missiles, cruise_missiles, unspecified_missiles, guided_aerial_bombs, tactic_aircraft_activity, strategic_aircraft_activity, mig31k_departure, air_defense, unknown}, threat level and started_at, source_message; UkraineAlarm activeAlertLevels[] with reason and createdAt. Threat features are only causally valid if logged live at time t by our own collector.
external_feature_timing: Live endpoints are near real-time (alerts.in.ua soft limit 8-10 req/min, hard 12 req/min per IP; history 2 req/min, not for real-time). updated_at gives a per-record change time, so a collector can reconstruct 'known at t' for ends, but not for edits made before the first fetch. UkraineAlarm via siren.pp.ua exhibited multi-minute publication lag in Sep 2026. For M6, end times observed only at the next daily pull must be treated as unknown until then (D-020 cap covers this).
split_scheme: Not applicable. Constraint for M6: alerts.in.ua history depth is 30 days, so a monthly job must persist every pull (datastore/alerts_in_ua.csv, D-016) or history is lost; a missed month cannot be backfilled from this API.
calibration_under_drift: Not applicable directly. The ecosystem itself documents the regime shift: alert_level red/yellow appeared with the Sep-2026 reform (v2 IoT R/Y codes; HA PR merged 2026-09-10; alerts-in-ua-py 0.4.0 on 2026-10-13). In our dump 63% of alerts are yellow (10,559 vs 6,180 red), so an 'any level' onset target in the new regime is not comparable in base rate to the pre-reform official target; supports D-015 exploratory framing.
regime_coverage: alerts.in.ua history only covers a rolling 30 days, so it can cover only the post-2026-09-06 yellow/red regime from the date pulls began; it cannot cover the Jan-2025 drone surge or the Dec-2025 raion reform. UkraineAlarm regionHistory (25 alerts/region) is too short for any regime analysis.
leakage_handling: Not applicable (APIs). Leakage-relevant properties: (a) history returns FINAL finished_at; using it to classify standing alerts at t leaks (D-020); (b) records can be updated after the fact (updated_at), so a dump is a post-hoc view; to be causal, keep each pull's fetch timestamp (manifest.tsv already records fetched_at_utc per UID) and dedupe by id with latest updated_at only for the training store, not for as-of-t reconstruction; (c) threats[] are point-in-time and disappear when closed, so any historical threat feature built from a later snapshot is impossible/leaky; (d) the Python client silently caches with If-Modified-Since and converts timezone; for reproducible dumps, store the raw JSON (as the project does) rather than client objects.
test_window_hygiene: Not applicable. Note: because the history window rolls daily, a new-regime evaluation must be pinned to a dated raw dump (data/raw/alerts_in_ua/2026-10-12T1645Z/) and never re-fetched live; re-fetching changes the window and the open-alert set.
headline_results: Not applicable (no models). Verified facts (2026-10-17): alerts.in.ua history limit 2 req/min (docs), general 8-10 soft / 12 hard req/min per IP, 429 on excess, token/IP blocking for systematic abuse; only month_ago documented; our dump 16,739 records over 26 UIDs, 0 duplicate ids, 41 open, yellow 63%, 289 non-air_raid rows. siren.pp.ua is live (35 regions with alerts, fresh lastUpdate 2026-10-17 13:05 UTC) and already returns activeAlertLevels Red/Yellow; api.ukrainealarm.com swagger returns 403/Cloudflare challenge to scripts (also reported in uasiren #6, open since 2025-09).
code_available: alerts-in-ua-py: MIT, active (0.4.0, 2026-10-13), sync (requests) + async clients, unit tests + opt-in live tests via ALERTS_IN_UA_TOKEN (same env var name as our project). uasiren: no license file, ~40-line aiohttp wrapper, unmaintained since 2022-05 but the siren.pp.ua service is live. PaulAnnekov/ukrainealarm: no license, unmaintained since 2022-05. UkraineAlarm-python: swagger-generated client (v3 API), key required.
takeaways_for_project: 1. Keep reading API data from the saved raw dump (CLAUDE.md data rule / D-015): the 30-day rolling window makes live re-fetch non-reproducible. 2. In load_api() (src/data.py) map to oblast via the requested UID from the filename or location_oblast name through src/regions.py, never via location_oblast_uid (wrong for 16,518 sub-oblast rows); add a raising data-quality check that each file's location_oblast is a single value matching the requested UID (D-017 item 6). 3. Filter alert_type == 'air_raid' explicitly and print the dropped count (289 in the dump); artillery_shelling/urban_fights rows would otherwise create spurious onsets in frontline hromadas. 4. Start the new-regime scored window after the earliest finished_at in the dump plus margin (current 2026-09-13 is consistent with min finished_at 2026-09-12 16:52 UTC) because of left-censoring; document this. 5. Keep open alerts (D-027) and rely on the D-020 cap; exclude Luhansk 16, Crimea 29, Sevastopol 30. 6. Red-only extra row (D-015 b): alert_level is per alert, while red threats can sit inside yellow alerts and threats[] are not in history, so state that 'red' = alert_level red, not 'missile threat'. 7. If the alerts_in_ua package is ever used (new dependency needs Oleksandr's approval), convert its Kyiv-aware datetimes back to UTC; the project's own raw-JSON reader avoids this. 8. M6 (future work, D-016): the monthly job must pull at most 2 history requests/min (24 oblast UIDs = about 12-13 min, as the 2026-10-12 dump took 15 min for 29 UIDs), run at least every ~25 days so the 30-day windows overlap, persist to datastore/alerts_in_ua.csv with fetch timestamps, dedupe by id with latest updated_at (D-027). 9. Do not substitute UkraineAlarm/siren.pp.ua as a history source: 25-alert history cap and a different channel; usable at most as a live cross-check, never mixed into a training set or metric.
best_practices: Adopt: store raw JSON per UID with HTTP status, bytes and fetch time (manifest.tsv pattern already in use); keep the token in env/.env and send it as a Bearer header, not a query string (docs allow both; query strings leak into logs); respect 2 req/min for history and use If-Modified-Since for live polling; treat 404 UIDs and empty files as explicit errors or documented exclusions, not silent skips; filter by alert_type; keep open alerts with a causal cap; record API/library version and dump timestamp in run_meta.json. Anti-patterns: trusting location_oblast_uid; using finished_at IS NULL as 'currently under alert'; computing onset rates from the first day of a rolling-window dump; building threat-type features from history; mixing alerts.in.ua with UkraineAlarm or the Telegram-derived official CSV; relying on an unmaintained keyless proxy (siren.pp.ua) for anything production-like; polling faster than the documented limits (risk of token/IP ban).
